summary: Module 7 CONTEXT micro-exercise (blame -> systems language). Rewrote the blame-full statement as blameless: 'The junior developer pushed untested code to production, causing the outage.' -> Blameless version: 'A code change was deployed to production without passing through the test suite. The deployment pipeline did not enforce test passage as a merge requirement, and the code review gate did not block unverified changes. The system therefore lacked a checkable invariant that production deployments only receive tested code.' Analysis: the person disappears; the verb is preserved as a system state ('deployed without passing tests'); the root cause moves to the pipeline (missing enforced gate), which is the only place a fix can live. If the rewrite still had a human subject ('the developer should have tested'), it would imply 'hire better developers' instead of 'fix the pipeline'. The blameless rewrite directs the remediation at structural checks (CI required-status, protected branch, review+test gate) that make the dangerous outcome harder to produce regardless of operator seniority -- exactly the S3 postmortem standard.
evidence: Blame-to-systems transformation: subject moved from person to pipeline
Remediation implied is structural (enforce test passage as merge requirement), not personnel
